test_title: PYST 28: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 24 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: If sin 3A = cos (A - 26º), then A = ______, where 3A is an acute angle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If sin x = cos y, then the sum of the angles is 90º (x + y = 90º).

⇒ 3A + (A − 26º) = 90º

⇒ 4A = 116º

⇒ A = 29º

**∴ The correct answer is 29º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin 3A = cos (A − 26º)

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = cos (90º − θ)

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos (90º − 3A) = cos (A − 26º)

Equating the angles since both are acute:

⇒ 90º − 3A = A − 26º

⇒ 4A = 90º + 26º

⇒ 4A = 116º

⇒ A = 116º ÷ 4

⇒ A = 29º

**∴ The correct answer is 29º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles Rule

When the sum of two angles is 90º, their sine and cosine values are equal. Examples: sin(90º − θ) = cos θ and cos(90º − θ) = sin θ.

Other Co-function Identities

tan(90º − θ) = cot θ and sec(90º − θ) = cosec θ.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.
